assessment: We index roughly 3% of the retailers a price-comparison site indexes. Our 8 are the specialist reloading houses, not the mass-market and regional retailers that dominate their list.
next_step: Do not chase all 273. Add retailers by RULE, not by count: major national chains first, then regional chains with real ammunition departments. AmmoSeek's own list names our missing set.

assessment: This is the honest headline: we have NO store-bought ammunition catalogue. Every product figure the competitor shows is a gap, and the reload-vs-buy verdict cannot be computed without a price side.
next_step: Build the ammunition-product schema with a purpose taxonomy, then seed a small SOURCED catalogue before scaling. Sourced beats large: 40 verifiable products beat 400 scraped ones we cannot defend.

assessment: They do not aggregate third-party product reviews, which is the clearest gap we have and the one explicitly permitted by 16 CFR 465.2(d)(2). Note the zero on both sides: this is an opening, not a race we are losing.
next_step: Build review ingestion with source licensing, attribution, observed conditions, and the 75k subscriber / 200k view floors with an observed_at date.

assessment: Neither side exposes a public historical price series, so the price-history gap is real but not uniquely winnable on data alone. Our advantage would be shipping history from day one rather than backfilling later.
next_step: Add the price time-series migration under the single-writer lock, and record price_observed_on on every listing from the first row onward so history accumulates.

assessment: Their component comparison covers 20+ retailers; we cover 8. Our sourcing_retailers table is deliberately small and cautious, with affiliate and scraping status recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
next_step: Add retailers only after reading each one's terms. scraping_status stays 'unknown' until someone has actually read them, because 'allowed' must never be assumed.

assessment: The one place we are ahead. We hold 318 cartridges against roughly 50 top calibers on their front page, because a cartridge record is reference data while their entries are product listings. Different things, not a win.
next_step: Keep the lead by adding CIP and NATO nomenclature from ammolytics/cartridges, and track the SAAMI free drawings for designs such as 8.6 Blackout and 30 Super Carry that post-date our data.
